chunks: I was ill for four months and did not perform voluntary prayers during them, so I mentioned that to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.
So he said: 'There is no making up upon you. Indeed, the sick person is not like the healthy one. Whatever Allah, Exalted is He, has caused to overcome him, then Allah is worthier of excusing him.'

key_terms.أَتَنَفَّلْ: I performed voluntary prayers; referring to nawafil
key_terms.الصَّحِيحِ: the healthy person; contrasted with the sick
key_terms.الْمَرِيضَ: the sick person; the subject of the ruling
key_terms.قَضَاءٌ: making up missed acts of worship afterward
key_terms.مَرِضْتُ: I became ill; indicating the state of sickness affecting worship

ai.seo_question: Does a sick person have to make up missed voluntary prayers in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that missed nawafil during illness do not require qaḍāʾ. It emphasizes that the condition of the sick differs from that of the healthy, and that when a matter is beyond a person's control by Allah's decree, divine excuse applies.
